This document collects the completed numbered ToDos attributable to Ed in
`ref-reports/edited-feedback-refine.md`. Items assigned to AK or left pending
are excluded. Text under **ToDo**, **Status**, and **Recorded output** is copied
from the source report. **Actual output located** adds the underlying generated
tables, figures, diagnostics, or manuscript changes found in the analysis and
paper repositories.

Links labeled **Where in the paper** open a review copy compiled from the
current Overleaf source at the relevant PDF page. Intermediate generated
`.tex`, CSV, and code-file links are intentionally omitted from this review
version.

# Detailed comment 1: Severe baseline imbalance in past deworming

## ToDo

> Check if previous worming is predictive of takeup in the paper (my guess no
> based on double lasso), bound TEs if so.
>
> Check definition of dewormed in the past year/dewormed in the past.
>
> Within 1,995 check if predictive within that sample.
>
> Use calendar as argument against:
>
> Before you move to your second step of bounding the treatment effect, you have
> a very powerful conceptual defense already in the paper: the Calendar arm. The
> baseline data shows that the Calendar arm has largely the same Far-Close
> imbalance in past deworming as the Bracelet and Ink arms. Yet, in the main
> results, the Calendar arm yields completely flat take-up across distance (it
> acts as a clean placebo). If the reviewer were correct that this specific
> baseline imbalance mechanically drives the take-up gap, the Calendar arm
> should have shown the same attenuated distance gradient as the public-signal
> arms. It did not.

## Status

> [DONE]

## Recorded output

> **Prior deworming experience.** The baseline survey also shows some arm
> differences in deworming knowledge and prior deworming experience (Appendix
> `Table~\ref{tab:baseline-bal}`). Because baseline survey records cannot be linked
> at the individual level to administrative take-up records, we address these
> differences by constructing community-level baseline shares for the imbalanced
> measures and merging them into the take-up and endline observability analyses.
> The results are stable. For administrative take-up, controlling for these
> baseline-survey community shares increases the Bracelet and Ink Far--Close
> interactions from 7.5 and 5.7 percentage points in the main specification to
> 12.1 and 10.7 percentage points, while the Calendar interaction remains small
> at 2.9 percentage points (`Appendix
> Table~\ref{tab:prior-deworming-robustness}`). For reported knowledge of peers'
> deworming status, the corresponding Far--Close interactions are nearly
> unchanged: 17.5 percentage points for Bracelet, 11.5 percentage points for
> Ink, and 2.4 percentage points for Calendar (`Appendix
> Table~\ref{tab:fob-baseline-imbalance-robustness}`). These checks suggest that
> the take-up and observability patterns are not driven by pre-existing
> differences in deworming knowledge or prior deworming experience across
> communities.

## Actual output located

The analysis produced both robustness tables referenced in the manuscript.

### Administrative take-up robustness

```{=latex}
\includepdf[pages=75,pagecommand={}]{ECM-ReStud-current.pdf}
```

### Observability robustness

```{=latex}
\includepdf[pages=70,pagecommand={}]{ECM-ReStud-current.pdf}
```

The tables show that the Bracelet and Ink Far--Close interactions remain
positive after adding the imbalanced baseline covariates, while the Calendar
interaction remains small.

**Where in the paper:** [Table B22, take-up robustness (p. 75)](ECM-ReStud-current.pdf#page=75)
and [Table B15, observability robustness (p. 70)](ECM-ReStud-current.pdf#page=70).

## Recorded output

## Actual output located

The Section 3.1 revision now states that the simulations condition on the fixed
surveyed-community frame and reproduce the PoT selection, Close/Far assignment,
targeted-community pairing, and feasibility restrictions. It concludes that
realized centroid-to-PoT distance can be interpreted as the continuous travel
distance variation induced by the design, conditional on that frame and the
constrained assignment protocol.
